subject: Error when trying to deploy to shinyapps.io: Application depends on package "package" but it is not

messages.author: 2fac004aeb6e2f8b
messages.subject: Error when trying to deploy to shinyapps.io: Application depends on package "package" but it is not
parts:
Hi everyone,

My server.R contains the following code for dynamically installing packages when needed:

package <- input$chip

if (!require(package, character.only=T, quietly=T)) {
      source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
      biocLite(package, ask = F, suppressUpdates = T, suppressAutoUpdate = T)
      library(package, character.only=T)
    }    
    
ui.R has a select input element where the user can select one of the following:

selectInput(inputId = 'chip', label='Chip', choices=c('Mouse Gene 1.0'='mogene10sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Mouse Gene 2.0'='mogene20sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Human Gene 1.0'='hugene10sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Human Genome U133A 2.0'='hgu133a2.db'))

So, based on what chip the user selects,  the corresponding annotation package should get loaded, and if not installed, it should install it. 

This works on my local machine. But when I try to deploy my app on shinyapps.io. I get the following error:

Error: 
* Application depends on package "package" but it is not installed. Please resolve before continuing.

I know that it is unable to recognize the 'package' in biocLite(package, ask = F, suppressUpdates = T, suppressAutoUpdate = T).  Is there any way to resolve this? Or do I have to explicitly load all required packages? 
The problem is that annotation packages are so big they take up a lot of memory, which is why I wanted to load these packages only when required. 

An alternative is to make an if-else loop or switch statement to install packages based on the condition, but I just wanted to know if this can work because this is so concise. 

Thanks!

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Error when trying to deploy to shinyapps.io: Application depends on package "package" but it is not
parts:
I might be wrong, but it looks to me like the deployment process thinks the name of the package is "package", which could be a bug since using the character.only parameter is not common so they might not have thought of that.  To see if this is indeed the issue, maybe try deploying something simple such as

mypkg <- "ggplot2"
library(mypkg , character.only = TRUE)

If that gives an error of "unable to deploy package 'mypkg'", then it's definitely a bug

My server.R contains the following code for dynamically installing packages when needed:

package <- input$chip

if (!require(package, character.only=T, quietly=T)) {
      source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
      biocLite(package, ask = F, suppressUpdates = T, suppressAutoUpdate = T)
      library(package, character.only=T)
    }    
    
ui.R has a select input element where the user can select one of the following:

selectInput(inputId = 'chip', label='Chip', choices=c('Mouse Gene 1.0'='mogene10sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Mouse Gene 2.0'='mogene20sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Human Gene 1.0'='hugene10sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Human Genome U133A 2.0'='hgu133a2.db'))

So, based on what chip the user selects,  the corresponding annotation package should get loaded, and if not installed, it should install it. 

This works on my local machine. But when I try to deploy my app on shinyapps.io. I get the following error:

Error: 
* Application depends on package "package" but it is not installed. Please resolve before continuing.

I know that it is unable to recognize the 'package' in biocLite(package, ask = F, suppressUpdates = T, suppressAutoUpdate = T).  Is there any way to resolve this? Or do I have to explicitly load all required packages? 
The problem is that annotation packages are so big they take up a lot of memory, which is why I wanted to load these packages only when required. 

An alternative is to make an if-else loop or switch statement to install packages based on the condition, but I just wanted to know if this can work because this is so concise. 

Thanks!

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Error when trying to deploy to shinyapps.io: Application depends on package "package" but it is not
parts:
Well, the shinyapps server that runs your code must install all the used libraries during deployment. They don't want to have to do dynamic package installation. So you do need to let shinyapps know about all the potential packages it needs when you deploy.

It sounds like your issue could be linked with this one
https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/issues/167

If there was a ShinySuggests field in the DESCRIPTION then you could list all the potential packages there without changing your code

---

On 2015-09-09 1:29 PM, "Komal Rathi" <komal...@gmail.com> wrote:
This did not give me any error but unfortunately my packages are bioconductor packages and not cran. 

On Wednesday, 9 September 2015 16:13:33 UTC-4, Dean Attali wrote:
I might be wrong, but it looks to me like the deployment process thinks the name of the package is "package", which could be a bug since using the character.only parameter is not common so they might not have thought of that.  To see if this is indeed the issue, maybe try deploying something simple such as

mypkg <- "ggplot2"
library(mypkg , character.only = TRUE)

If that gives an error of "unable to deploy package 'mypkg'", then it's definitely a bug
